successors.name: Tokugawa shogunate
successors.text: the Osaka fief of Hideyori: Osaka Castle and its 650,000 koku

ledger.x: 2 July 1582: Yamazaki.
1583: Shizugatake.
1583: 'Terumoto became a vassal of Toyotomi Hideyoshi' after the 1582 peace.
1584: Komaki and Nagakute.
1584: the stalemate with Ieyasu; the pages give no treaty.
After 1584: Hideyoshi 'became ruler of the former Oda domains'.
June 1585: Hideyoshi assembled 113,000 men in three armies; Chōsokabe had about 40,000 to defend Shikoku, which he controlled (Iyo, Sanuki, Awa, Tosa) in 1583.
6 August 1585 (11th day of the 7th month of Tenshō 13): Chōsokabe surrendered.
6 August 1585: Awa to Hachisuka Iemasa and Akamatsu Norifusa, Sanuki to Sengoku Hidehisa and Sogō Masayasu, Iyo to Kobayakawa Takakage and other Mōri generals.
6 August 1585: 'Chōsokabe was allowed to keep Tosa Province.'
1587: Hidenaga landed south of Bungo and attacked the Shimazu at Takajō in Hyūga.
Later in 1587: the Shimazu surrendered; 'Kagoshima itself was not attacked'.

1587 settlement: the Shimazu, who by mid-1585 controlled Chikugo, Chikuzen, Hizen, Higo, Hyūga, Ōsumi and Satsuma, kept only Satsuma, Ōsumi and half of Hyūga; 'most conquered domains went to Katō, Konishi, and…
June 1587: Yoshihisa 'sued for peace' after the Shimazu were routed in Satsuma; they kept Satsuma, 'Ōsumi Province' and half of Hyūga.
1590: Hideyoshi 'forced the clans of the Tōhoku region to swear allegiance to him'; the Senboku uprising against the Taikō survey followed in September and the Kunohe rebellion in Mutsu.
May 1590: the siege of Odawara, 220,000 Toyotomi men against 82,000.
4 August 1590: the siege ends; the defenders surrendered after three months when Ishigakiyama Ichiya Castle appeared.
4 August 1590: Odawara.
1600: Ieyasu 'seized control' after Sekigahara and deposed Hideyori; the tokugawa-clan dossier closes in October 1600.
1600: after Sekigahara Ieyasu 'reduced his domains, leaving him only Nagato and Suō Provinces, worth 369,000 koku'; the vassalage to the Toyotomi ends with Ieyasu's seizure of control.
1600: Ieyasu 'seized control' after Sekigahara and deposed Hideyori.
1600: the same bridging; the Satsuma Domain dossier dates the Edo domain from 1600.
1600: the same bridging; no page gives Tōhoku's position after Sekigahara.
1600: 'Tokugawa Ieyasu seized control in 1600, after his victory over the others at the Battle of Sekigahara'; the Toyotomi clan page: Hideyori was deposed that year.
8 November 1614: the winter campaign begins (4 December: siege of Osaka Castle).
22 January 1615: peace terms sworn by Hideyori; the outer and inner moats were filled.
May 1615: the summer campaign (Kashii 26 May, Dōmyōji 2 June); Hideyori's March 1615 request for a neighbouring province was refused.
June 1615: Osaka Castle falls; Hideyori and Yodo-dono commit seppuku in the flames.
June 1615: 'Tokugawa victory'; the Toyotomi clan destroyed; Hideyori died on 4 June and the summer siege is dated 5 June 1615 in the Hideyori text.

wars.name: Battle of Shizugatake
wars.outcome: Hideyoshi won; Kitanoshō fell and Shibata Katsuie killed himself; Oda Nobutaka was forced to suicide in June 1583.

wars.name: Battle of Komaki and Nagakute
wars.outcome: Inconclusive; no territory change on the pages.

wars.name: Invasion of Shikoku
wars.outcome: Chōsokabe surrendered on 6 August 1585 and kept Tosa; the rest of Shikoku was given to Hideyoshi's men.

wars.name: Kyūshū campaign
wars.outcome: The Shimazu were driven back from Hyūga and surrendered in 1587; Kagoshima was not attacked.

wars.name: Siege of Odawara
wars.outcome: The Hōjō surrendered on 4 August 1590; Ujimasa was later forced to suicide; Ieyasu was given the Hōjō lands.

wars.name: Kunohe rebellion
wars.outcome: Ran 13 March to 4 September 1591 in Mutsu; Hideyoshi and Ieyasu defeated Kunohe Masazane.

wars.name: Japanese invasions of Korea
wars.outcome: Seoul by May 1592 and Pyongyang within three months; withdrawn to the south of the peninsula by January 1593; a second invasion in 1597 failed; the Japanese withdrew after Hideyoshi's death in September 1598.

wars.name: Sekigahara campaign
wars.outcome: The Eastern Army under Ieyasu defeated the Western Army of Toyotomi loyalists (Sengoku page); Hideyori was deposed.

wars.name: Siege of Osaka
wars.outcome: Winter campaign (8 November 1614 to 22 January 1615) ended in a peace; the summer campaign (May-June 1615) ended with the fall of Osaka Castle and the Toyotomi's end.

certainty.note: The pages name castles and provinces, not borders; the Toyotomi hegemony over the daimyo is drawn only where a page names the land, and the Chūgoku, Hokuriku and Kinai lands are not named.
